verdict: Applied Digital's revenue quadrupled to $341.9M as its AI data-center business took off, but heavy interest costs, fair-value losses and stock pay left a $184.1M consolidated net loss.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP, attributable)
kpis.note: Per share loss for common stockholders; continuing operations were -$0.76

kpis.label: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.note: The company's non-GAAP measure, excluding its ChronoScale subsidiary

kpis.label: Contracted leases
kpis.note: About 1.41 GW of leased capacity across five campuses, over the initial lease terms

segments.name: HPC Hosting
segments.note: Purpose-built AI data centers ('AI factories') leased to hyperscalers: $65.8M of base rent, $183.5M of tenant fit-out work and $13.3M of tenant recoveries. Segment profit was $33.4M.

segments.name: ChronoScale (cloud services)
segments.note: The majority-owned accelerated-compute (GPU cloud) business, consolidated here but excluded from the company's adjusted figures.

segments.name: Data Center Hosting
segments.note: Energized data-center space for crypto-mining customers in North Dakota, running at full capacity. Segment profit was $13.3M.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Running and building the company, including $59.4M of stock-based pay across the business and deal and diligence costs. Much of it is not allocated to the segments.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $77.383M, a $49.511M loss on the change in fair value of derivatives and an $11.352M loss on the change in fair value of an investment, plus $1.311M of other expense, partly offset by $35.821M of interest income — and a $16.054M loss from discontinued operations — for net other expense of $119.790M.

takeaways.title: The AI factory business arrived
takeaways.text: Revenue jumped from $80.9M to $341.9M. HPC Hosting — data centers built for AI tenants — produced $262.6M, mostly $183.5M of tenant fit-out work plus the first full quarters of rent. The two reported segments together earned $46.8M of segment profit.

takeaways.title: Head-office costs swamped segment profit
takeaways.text: Consolidated operating result was a $62.4M loss, because $114.7M of general and administrative costs — including $59.4M of stock-based pay — sit above the segment lines. Excluding ChronoScale and one-offs, the company's adjusted operating income was $37.8M.

takeaways.title: Financing the build-out is expensive
takeaways.text: Interest expense was $77.4M in one quarter, and mark-to-market losses on derivatives and an investment added another $60.9M. After a $16.1M discontinued-operations loss, the consolidated net loss was $184.1M; the loss attributable to common stockholders was $237.1M after preferred dividends and the noncontrolling share.

oneTimers: Losses on the change in fair value of derivatives ($49.5M) and of an investment ($11.4M) are non-cash mark-to-market moves, not operating costs.
A $16.1M loss from discontinued operations is included in other expense in the flow below so the bottom line is the full consolidated net loss; continuing operations lost $168.0M.
footerNote: Applied Digital reports in thousands; figures are shown in $M with decimals so the lines add up exactly. Cost of revenue combines its two reported cost lines (services $245.709M and data-center rental $43.862M). This is a loss quarter: the shortfall is covered by cash on hand and new financing.
